events.title: Martin Luther Posts the Ninety-Five Theses
events.description: According to tradition, German monk and theologian Martin Luther posted his Ninety-Five Theses on the door of the Castle Church in Wittenberg, criticizing the Catholic Church's sale of indulgences.
events.significance: This act is widely regarded as the starting point of the Protestant Reformation, which permanently divided Western Christianity and reshaped the political and cultural landscape of Europe.

events.title: Nevada Admitted as the 36th U.S. State
events.description: During the American Civil War, President Abraham Lincoln proclaimed Nevada a state, admitting it to the Union just days before the 1864 presidential election.
events.significance: Nevada's admission added mineral wealth, particularly silver from the Comstock Lode, and additional electoral support for the Union cause. It earned Nevada the nickname 'Battle Born.'

events.title: Completion of Mount Rushmore
events.description: After 14 years of construction, work on the Mount Rushmore National Memorial in South Dakota officially ended. Sculptor Gutzon Borglum designed it, and his son Lincoln finished it after Gutzon's death in March 1941. It depicts Presidents Washington, Jefferson, Theodore Roosevelt, and Lincoln.
events.significance: Mount Rushmore became one of the most recognizable American monuments and a major tourist destination, though it remains controversial because it was carved into the Black Hills, land sacred to the Lakota Sioux.

events.title: Assassination of Indira Gandhi
events.description: Indian Prime Minister Indira Gandhi was assassinated in New Delhi by two of her Sikh bodyguards, in retaliation for Operation Blue Star, the military action at the Golden Temple in Amritsar earlier that year.
events.significance: Her death led to widespread anti-Sikh riots in which thousands were killed, and brought her son Rajiv Gandhi to power. It remains a defining moment in modern Indian political history.
